speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: asked the Minister for Manpower what will be the impact of wage cuts in the next 12 months given the recent announcement by the National Wages Council that employers can consider temporarily cutting workers' basic pay if necessary to stave off retrenchments.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Not every employer will need to cut wages to save jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Some have seen no reduction in demand and thus have no reason to make wage cuts.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Others have already adjusted wage levels or non-wage costs, in line with the Guidelines issued in March.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The NWC also expects that employers will deliberate carefully whether to proceed with a wage cut.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Employers will also be mindful that unwarranted wage cuts will make them less attractive to their workers and they will risk losing talent.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The NWC has also clearly marked out a roadmap for the eventual wage restoration.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Employers are to quickly restore wage cuts accepted in good faith by employees when business conditions allow them to do so.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: I appreciate that the companies are impacted in an uneven way during this COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: But the National Wages Council Guidelines for employers to implement temporary wage cuts to save jobs is actually too broad and left too much to the discretion of the businesses.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: For example, indicators for companies' efforts to reduce non-wage costs before wage adjustment, or company profitability, and market and economic indicators.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: I have a second supplementary question to this.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: For lower wage workers who are impacted by the wage reduction, will the Government consider a Workfare special payment to cushion the pay cut in order to ensure that these families have a basic level of income to sustain their daily living?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: At the same time, I think the NWC in its deliberations has also got to consider the flipside, which is that its Guidelines could be too prescriptive and too one-size-fits-all.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, I think between the two, both of which are equally difficult, they have to strike a balance.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To share with the Member, the NWC very carefully deliberated whether they should even go into, for example, sector-specific Guidelines.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Meaning to prescribe a certain range of adjustments that could be applicable on a sectoral basis.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And after intense deliberation, the NWC came to the conclusion that even sectoral Guidelines would be too one-size-fits-all.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That is because within the same sectors, we have companies that have been impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic to different degrees.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And so, the Guidelines on a sectoral basis could be too generous for some companies and too tight for some others.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I give you the example of the logistics sector.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If the companies are, for example, serving the aviation and the aerospace or hospitality related industries, then, these logistics companies would be impacted to a larger degree.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But if they are serving the e-commerce or some aspects of manufacturing, they could still be doing very well, for example, in healthcare and pharmaceutical.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The presence of the Flexible Wage System differs from company to company.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Some companies have implemented the Annual Variable Component and on top of that, they also have the Monthly Variable Component.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, those are the components that should be used first.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The second principle is that if an employer has not adopted a Flexible Wage System, then any adjustments that they make to wages should then constitute a new variable component in the employer's pay structure.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The third principle is for the management to take earlier and deeper wage cuts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think this applies across the board and is well understood. the fourth principle is that employers who already pay Annual Wage Supplement, should endeavour to continue to do so.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The NWC was not vague about it at all.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The fifth principle is that in deciding on the reasonable level of wage cuts, employer should take into account a couple of factors.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For example, the sector and the company's performance and outlook.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It should take into account the level of Government support that it has already received or it is about to receive.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It should take into account the cumulative effect of prior wage cuts and other cost-saving measures that have been implemented.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It should take into account the impact on the employees' finances and also the employees continue to contribute full or longer working hours.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In other words, this particular criterion already has quite a lot of dimensions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In other words, to share information, to exchange an understanding of where the company is right now, in coming to an agreement to what the wage adjustments should be.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think whilst I understand where the Member is coming from, if the NWC were to go beyond this, I suspect that we would say that it has become too prescriptive and not providing sufficient flexibility for different circumstances across firms and across sectors.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, it is a delicate balance and I know that it is not easy for them to strike.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Given that all the tripartite partners were involved in this discussion, they came out with a set of Guidelines that I think were reasonable and something that on the part of the union, they also felt that they could operate on this basis.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Member's second question with regard to Workfare special payment, I appreciate her concern for our lower wage workers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the considerations for next year's Budget, I am very certain that the Ministries of Finance and Manpower will work very closely together to see how best to support our lower-wage workers.
